442: ## 7. WORKFLOW PATTERNS
443: 
444: **Purpose**: Show how to represent multi-step workflows using YAML structures.
445: 
446: ### YAML Pipeline: Document Creation Workflow
447: 
448: **Before (Markdown List)**:
449: ```markdown
450: 1. Analyze the request and determine document type
451: 2. Select appropriate template
452: 3. Populate template with content
453: 4. Validate structure and content
454: 5. Apply formatting standards
455: 6. Run quality checks
456: ```
457: 
458: **After (YAML Pipeline)**:
459: ```yaml
460: document_creation_workflow:
461:   phase_1_analysis:
462:     action: "Analyze request and determine document type"
463:     output: "Document type classification"
464:     validation: "Type must be one of: SKILL, Command, Knowledge, Spec, README"
465: 
466:   phase_2_template_selection:
467:     action: "Select appropriate template based on document type"
468:     output: "Template file path"
469:     depends_on: "phase_1_analysis"
470: 
471:   phase_3_population:
472:     action: "Populate template with user-provided content"
473:     output: "Draft document with filled sections"
474:     depends_on: "phase_2_template_selection"
475: 
476:   phase_4_validation:
477:     action: "Validate structure, frontmatter, section ordering"
478:     output: "Validation report (errors/warnings)"
479:     depends_on: "phase_3_population"
480: 
481:   phase_5_formatting:
482:     action: "Apply code standards (spacing, headers)"
483:     output: "Formatted document"
484:     depends_on: "phase_4_validation"
485: 
486:   phase_6_quality_check:
487:     action: "Review checklist + run AI quality evaluation"
488:     output: "Quality notes and improvement recommendations"
489:     depends_on: "phase_5_formatting"
490: ```
491: 
492: ### YAML Configuration: Feature Flags
493: 
494: **Before (Markdown Table)**:
495: ```markdown
496: | Feature           | Default | Description                         |
497: | ----------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------- |
498: | strict_validation | true    | Enforce all validation rules        |
499: | auto_fix          | false   | Automatically fix formatting issues |
500: | frontmatter_check | true    | Validate frontmatter per document type |
501: ```
502: 
503: **After (YAML Configuration)**:
504: ```yaml
505: feature_flags:
506:   strict_validation:
507:     default: true
508:     description: "Enforce all validation rules without warnings"
509:     values: [true, false]
510: 
511:   auto_fix:
512:     default: false
513:     description: "Automatically fix formatting issues during validation"
514:     values: [true, false]
515:     warning: "Use with caution - may change document semantics"
516: 
517:   frontmatter_check:
518:     default: true
519:     description: "Validate frontmatter fields per document type"
520:     values: [true, false]
521:     enforcement_level: "error"
522: ```
523: 
524: ### YAML Workflow: Multi-Branch Decision Process
525: 
526: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
527: ```markdown
528: The system should detect when to generate variants:
529: - If user explicitly requests options (shows me options, variations, different approaches)
530: - If complexity is high (7+) and uncertainty signals are present (not sure, what would work)
531: - Otherwise, generate single solution
532: 
533: Variant count depends on complexity:
534: - Simple: 2-3 variants
535: - Standard: 3-5 variants
536: - Complex: 5-10 variants
537: ```
538: 
539: **After (YAML Multi-Branch)**:
540: ```yaml
541: variant_generation_logic:
542:   triggers:
543:     explicit:
544:       keywords: ["show me options", "variations", "different approaches", "multiple designs"]
545:       action: "Generate variants immediately"
546:       priority: "high"
547: 
548:     implicit:
549:       conditions:
550:         - "complexity >= 7"
551:         - "uncertainty_signals present"
552:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work", "best approach"]
553:       action: "Generate variants with uncertainty disclaimer"
554:       priority: "medium"
555: 
556:     default:
557:       action: "Generate single optimal solution"
558:       priority: "low"
559: 
560:   variant_count_guidelines:
561:     simple:
562:       complexity_range: [1, 3]
563:       variant_count: "2-3"
564: 
565:     standard:
566:       complexity_range: [4, 6]
567:       variant_count: "3-5"
568: 
569:     complex:
570:       complexity_range: [7, 10]
571:       variant_count: "5-10"
572: 
573:     user_specified:
574:       action: "Honor user's requested count"
575:       override: true
576: ```

675: ## 9. TEMPLATE GUIDELINES
676: 
677: ### Naming Conventions
678: 
679: **File Names** (kebab-case required):
680: - Format: `[topic]-[type].md`
681: - Use hyphens, not underscores
682: - Lowercase only
683: - Descriptive and specific
684: - Examples:
685:   - ✅ `frontmatter-templates.md`
686:   - ✅ `validation-reference.md`
687:   - ✅ `config-examples.yaml`
688:   - ✅ `packaging-guide.md`
689:   - ❌ `templates.md` (too generic)
690:   - ❌ `FrontmatterTemplates.md` (wrong case)
691:   - ❌ `frontmatter_templates.md` (underscores are not canonical)
692: 
693: **Type-Specific Patterns**:
694: 
695: | Asset Type | Naming Pattern           | Kebab-case Examples          |
696: | ---------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
697: | Template   | `[content]-templates.md` | `frontmatter-templates.md`   |
698: | Reference  | `[topic]-reference.md`   | `emoji-reference.md`         |
699: | Example    | `[topic]-examples.md`    | `optimization-examples.md`   |
700: | Guide      | `[process]-guide.md`     | `packaging-guide.md`         |
701: | Checklist  | `[topic]-checklist.md`   | `validation-checklist.md`    |
702: 
703: **Section Names**:
704: - Use title case
705: - Be descriptive but concise
706: - Number if sequential: `1. Template Name`
707: 
708: ### Content Organization
709: 
710: **Progressive Disclosure**:
711: 1. **Introduction**: What this is, why it exists (1-2 sentences)
712: 2. **Sections**: Each covers one topic completely
713: 3. **Examples**: Show, don't just tell
714: 4. **Quick Reference**: Summary at end (optional)
715: 
716: **Section Structure**:
717: - **Purpose**: Why this section exists
718: - **Guidelines**: How to use the content
719: - **Template**: Copy-paste starting point
720: - **Example**: Complete working example
721: 
722: ### Formatting Standards
723: 
724: **Code Blocks**:
725: - Always specify language: ` ```yaml `, ` ```markdown `, ` ```bash `
726: - Include comments explaining non-obvious parts
727: - Show complete, runnable examples
728: - Use placeholder values that are obviously placeholders
729: 
730: **Placeholders**:
731: - Format: `[descriptive-name]` or `your-value-here`
732: - Examples:
733:   - ✅ `[skill-name]`, `[feature-description]`, `your-project-name`
734:   - ❌ `xxx`, `placeholder`, `FIXME`
735: 
736: **Lists**:
737: - Use `-` for unordered lists
738: - Use `1.` for ordered lists
739: - Nested lists indent by 2 spaces
740: - Keep items parallel in structure
741: 
742: **Tables**:
743: - Include header row
744: - Align consistently (usually left-aligned)
745: - Keep rows concise (1-2 lines)
746: - Use for comparisons or reference data
747: 
748: ### Writing Style
749: 
750: **Clarity**:
751: - Write for someone unfamiliar with your skill
752: - Define domain-specific terms on first use
753: - Use active voice: "Create the file" not "The file should be created"
754: - Be concise but complete
755: 
756: **Examples**:
757: - Every template should have a complete example
758: - Show real-world usage, not toy examples
759: - Include common variations
760: - Annotate non-obvious parts
761: 
762: **Consistency**:
763: - Use same terminology throughout
764: - Follow patterns from other assets in the skill
765: - Match style of SKILL.md
766: - Use consistent formatting

14: # Skill Asset File Templates - Creation Guidelines
15: 
16: Templates and guidelines for creating asset files in AI agent skills.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### Location & Naming
21: 
22: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/assets/`
23: 
24: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with the appropriate extension
25: 
26: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
27: |---------------|-----------------|
28: | `frontmatter-templates.md` | `FrontmatterTemplates.md` (PascalCase) |
29: | `config-examples.yaml` | `config_examples.yaml` (snake_case) |
30: | `validation-checklist.md` | `ValidationChecklist.MD` (wrong case) |
31: | `emoji-reference.md` | `emojiReference.md` (camelCase) |
32: 
33: ### When to Create Assets
34: 
35: **Create an asset file when:**
36: - Templates users apply repeatedly
37: - Reference data >50 lines and self-contained
38: - Multiple examples of same pattern exist
39: - Lookup tables or decision matrices needed
40: - Template variations for different scenarios
41: 
42: **Keep in SKILL.md when:**
43: - Content <30 lines
44: - Tightly coupled to workflow logic
45: - Needs to be visible immediately (not progressive disclosure)
46: - Part of core instructions (RULES, WORKFLOW sections)
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 2. ASSET FILE TYPES
51: 
52: ### Template Files
53: **Purpose**: Provide copy-paste starting points for common tasks
54: 
55: **Naming**: `[content-type]-templates.md`
56: - Example: `frontmatter-templates.md`, `structure-templates.md`
57: 
58: **Structure**:
59: - One template per section
60: - Include field descriptions
61: - Show complete examples
62: - Explain when to use each template
63: 
64: **Use cases**:
65: - Document templates (SKILL.md, commands, knowledge files)
66: - Configuration templates (YAML, JSON)
67: - Code templates (functions, classes, modules)
68: 
69: ### Reference Files
70: **Purpose**: Provide lookup tables, decision trees, or reference data
71: 
72: **Naming**: `[topic]-reference.md`
73: - Example: `emoji-reference.md`, `validation-reference.md`
74: 
75: **Structure**:
76: - Tables or lists for quick lookup
77: - Decision matrices
78: - Classification systems
79: - Standards and conventions
80: 
81: **Use cases**:
82: - Emoji selection guides
83: - File type classifications
84: - Validation rule sets
85: - Naming conventions
86: 
87: ### Example Files
88: **Purpose**: Show working examples of skill outputs
89: 
90: **Naming**: `[topic]-examples.md`
91: - Example: `optimization-examples.md`, `skill-examples.md`
92: 
93: **Structure**:
94: - Before/after comparisons
95: - Annotated examples
96: - Multiple variations
97: - Anti-patterns to avoid
98: 
99: **Use cases**:
100: - Complete skill applications
101: - Common patterns
102: - Edge cases
103: - Quality standards
104: 
105: ### Guide Files
106: **Purpose**: Detailed how-to guides for complex processes
107: 
108: **Naming**: `[process]-guide.md`
109: - Example: `packaging-guide.md`, `distribution-guide.md`
110: 
111: **Structure**:
112: - Step-by-step instructions
113: - Troubleshooting sections
114: - Best practices
115: - Common pitfalls
116: 
117: **Use cases**:
118: - Multi-step processes
119: - Advanced techniques
120: - Workflow deep-dives
121: - Integration guides
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## 3. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
126: 
127: ### Title and Intro
128: 
129: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
130: 
131: ```markdown
132: ---
133: title: [Title]
134: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
135: trigger_phrases:
136:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
137:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
138:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
139: importance_tier: normal
140: contextType: general
141: version: 1.0.0.0
142: ---
143: 
144: # [Title]
145: 
146: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
147: 
148: \## 1. OVERVIEW
149: 
150: ### Purpose
151: 
152: [Why this asset exists]
153: 
154: ### Usage
155: 
156: [How to use this asset - copy instructions, customization notes]
157: 
158: ---
159: 
160: \## 2. [Content Section]
161: 
162: [The actual template/checklist/snippet content]
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## N. Related Resources (optional, if present must be last)
167: 
168: [Links to related files]
169: 
170: ```
171: 
172: Every asset file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content, `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, and `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
173: 
174: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and OVERVIEW section.**
175: > The intro is a hook. OVERVIEW provides the details.
176: 
177: #### GOOD Intro Structure
178: 
179: ```markdown
180: # Git Commit Templates
181: 
182: Copy the template that matches the change, fill the fields, and commit.
183: 
184: \## 1. OVERVIEW
185: 
186: ### Purpose
187: 
188: Uniform messages let a reader scan history by intent instead of by author.
189: 
190: ### Usage
191: 
192: Copy the appropriate template based on commit type...
193: 
194: ---
195: 
196: \## 2. COMMIT TEMPLATES
197: ...
198: ```
199: 
200: #### BAD Intro Structure (too long, has subsections)
201: 
202: ```markdown
203: # Git Commit Templates
204: 
205: Copy-paste templates for creating well-structured commit messages.
206: 
207: ### Core Principle    ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
208: Atomic commits with clear intent = maintainable history.
209: 
210: ### When to Use       ← WRONG: This belongs in OVERVIEW section!
211: - Creating new features
212: - Fixing bugs
213: 
214: ---
215: ```
216: 
217: ### Intro vs OVERVIEW Content Placement
218: 
219: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | OVERVIEW Section       |
220: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- |
221: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat)    |
222: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Purpose)     |
223: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Purpose)     |
224: | How to copy/customize | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Usage)       |
225: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Usage)       |
226: | Any H2/H3 subsections | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES                  |
227: 
228: ---
229: 
230: ## 4. STANDARD ASSET STRUCTURE
231: 
232: **Template**:
233: 
234: ````markdown
235: ---
236: title: Asset Title - Descriptive Subtitle
237: description: One-line description of what this asset provides
238: trigger_phrases:
239:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
240:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
241:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
242: importance_tier: normal
243: contextType: general
244: version: 1.0.0.0
245: ---
246: 
247: # Asset Title - Descriptive Subtitle
248: 
249: Brief introduction (1-2 sentences) explaining what this asset provides and when to use it.
250: 
251: \## 1. OVERVIEW
252: 
253: ### Purpose
254: 
255: [Why this asset exists, what problem it solves]
256: 
257: ### Usage
258: 
259: [How to use this asset - copy instructions, customization notes]
260: 
261: ---
262: 
263: \## 2. SECTION NAME
264: 
265: **Key Points**:
266: - Point 1
267: - Point 2
268: - Point 3
269: 
270: **Template**:
271: ```[language]
272: # Template content here
273: # With explanatory comments
274: ```
275: 
276: **Field Guidelines**:
277: 
278: **`field_name`**:
279: - Description of field
280: - Format requirements
281: - Example: `value-example`
282: 
283: **Complete Example**:
284: ```[language]
285: # Complete working example
286: # Ready to copy and adapt
287: ```
288: 
289: ---
290: 
291: \## 3. SECTION NAME
292: 
293: [Continue pattern...]
294: 
295: ---
296: 
297: ## N. RELATED RESOURCES
298: 
299: [Links to related files - MUST be last section if present]
300: 
301: ````
302: 
303: ---
304: 
305: ## 5. LOGIC REPRESENTATION PATTERNS
306: 
307: **Purpose**: Guidelines for representing logic, workflows, and decision trees in asset files using structured formats instead of prose.
308: 
309: **Why Structured Logic?**
310: - **Clarity**: Executable-style logic is easier to understand than prose
311: - **AI-Friendly**: LLMs parse structured logic better than narrative descriptions
312: - **Maintainability**: Changes to logic are more visible in structured formats
313: - **Consistency**: Same patterns across all asset files
314: 
315: ### When to Use Each Format
316: 
317: **Use Python Pseudo-Code When:**
318: - Complex branching logic (multiple IF/ELIF/ELSE conditions)
319: - Function/method definitions with clear inputs/outputs
320: - State management or algorithmic processes
321: - Validation or transformation logic
322: - Examples: Mode detection, validation pipelines, decision functions
323: 
324: **Use YAML Structures When:**
325: - Configuration data (settings, options, parameters)
326: - Pipeline definitions (multi-step workflows with clear phases)
327: - Hierarchical workflows (nested processes)
328: - Metadata structures (categorization, tagging)
329: - Examples: Workflow definitions, configuration templates, feature matrices
330: 
331: **Use Markdown Decision Trees When:**
332: - Simple branching logic (2-5 branches)
333: - Visual flow representation (user-facing paths)
334: - Classification systems (type determination)
335: - Quick decision guides
336: - Examples: Document type selection, frontmatter requirements
337: 
338: **Keep Markdown Prose When:**
339: - Explanatory text and conceptual overviews
340: - Narrative examples with context
341: - Best practices guidance
342: - Introductions and summaries
343: 
344: ---
345: 
346: ## 6. DECISION LOGIC EXAMPLES
347: 
348: **Purpose**: Demonstrate how to convert markdown prose into structured decision logic.
349: 
350: ### Python Pseudo-Code: Mode Detection
351: 
352: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
353: ```markdown
354: Check user input for mode indicators:
355: - If "$quick" is present, use quick mode with auto-scaling depth
356: - If "$ticket" is present, use ticket mode with depth 10
357: - Otherwise, use interactive mode with depth 10
358: ```
359: 
360: **After (Python Pseudo-Code)**:
361: ```python
362: def detect_mode(request):
363:     """Detect execution mode from user request markers"""
364: 
365:     if '$quick' in request:
366:         mode = 'quick'
367:         depth = 'auto_scale_1_to_5'
368:     elif '$ticket' in request:
369:         mode = 'ticket'
370:         depth = 'depth_10_rounds'
371:     else:
372:         # DEFAULT TO INTERACTIVE
373:         mode = 'interactive'
374:         depth = 'depth_10_rounds'
375: 
376:     return mode, depth
377: ```
378: 
379: ### Markdown Decision Tree: Frontmatter Requirements
380: 
381: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
382: ```markdown
383: Different document types have different frontmatter requirements:
384: - SKILL.md files must have frontmatter with name, description, allowed-tools, and version
385: - Command files must have frontmatter with description and argument-hint
386: - Skill reference/asset files must have the 5-field block
387: - Knowledge files outside skill folders should not have frontmatter
388: - Spec files typically don't have frontmatter
389: ```
390: 
391: **After (Markdown Decision Tree)**:
392: ```
393: Document type?
394: ├─> SKILL.md             → MUST have frontmatter (name, description, allowed-tools, version)
395: ├─> Command              → MUST have frontmatter (description, argument-hint, allowed-tools)
396: ├─> Skill Reference/Asset → MUST have the 5-field block (title, description,
397: │                           trigger_phrases, importance_tier, contextType)
398: ├─> Knowledge (outside skills) → MUST NOT have frontmatter (remove if present)
399: ├─> Spec                 → SHOULD NOT have frontmatter (suggest removal)
400: └─> README               → No specific requirement (usually none)
401: ```
402: 
403: ### Python Pseudo-Code: Validation Logic
404: 
405: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
406: ```markdown
407: Validate the document structure:
408: 1. Check if required sections exist
409: 2. Verify section ordering is correct
410: 3. Ensure frontmatter is valid (if present)
411: ```
412: 
413: **After (Python Pseudo-Code)**:
414: ```python
415: def validate_document(doc, doc_type):
416:     """Validate document structure and content"""
417: 
418:     errors = []
419: 
420:     # Check required sections
421:     required_sections = get_required_sections(doc_type)
422:     for section in required_sections:
423:         if section not in doc.sections:
424:             errors.append(f"Missing required section: {section}")
425: 
426:     # Verify section ordering
427:     expected_order = get_section_order(doc_type)
428:     actual_order = [s.name for s in doc.sections]
429:     if actual_order != expected_order:
430:         errors.append(f"Section order incorrect. Expected: {expected_order}")
431: 
432:     # Validate frontmatter
433:     if doc.has_frontmatter:
434:         frontmatter_errors = validate_frontmatter(doc.frontmatter, doc_type)
435:         errors.extend(frontmatter_errors)
436: 
437:     return errors
438: ```
439: 
440: ---
441: 
442: ## 7. WORKFLOW PATTERNS
443: 
444: **Purpose**: Show how to represent multi-step workflows using YAML structures.
445: 
446: ### YAML Pipeline: Document Creation Workflow
447: 
448: **Before (Markdown List)**:
449: ```markdown
450: 1. Analyze the request and determine document type
451: 2. Select appropriate template
452: 3. Populate template with content
453: 4. Validate structure and content
454: 5. Apply formatting standards
455: 6. Run quality checks
456: ```
457: 
458: **After (YAML Pipeline)**:
459: ```yaml
460: document_creation_workflow:
461:   phase_1_analysis:
462:     action: "Analyze request and determine document type"
463:     output: "Document type classification"
464:     validation: "Type must be one of: SKILL, Command, Knowledge, Spec, README"
465: 
466:   phase_2_template_selection:
467:     action: "Select appropriate template based on document type"
468:     output: "Template file path"
469:     depends_on: "phase_1_analysis"
470: 
471:   phase_3_population:
472:     action: "Populate template with user-provided content"
473:     output: "Draft document with filled sections"
474:     depends_on: "phase_2_template_selection"
475: 
476:   phase_4_validation:
477:     action: "Validate structure, frontmatter, section ordering"
478:     output: "Validation report (errors/warnings)"
479:     depends_on: "phase_3_population"
480: 
481:   phase_5_formatting:
482:     action: "Apply code standards (spacing, headers)"
483:     output: "Formatted document"
484:     depends_on: "phase_4_validation"
485: 
486:   phase_6_quality_check:
487:     action: "Review checklist + run AI quality evaluation"
488:     output: "Quality notes and improvement recommendations"
489:     depends_on: "phase_5_formatting"
490: ```
491: 
492: ### YAML Configuration: Feature Flags
493: 
494: **Before (Markdown Table)**:
495: ```markdown
496: | Feature           | Default | Description                         |
497: | ----------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------- |
498: | strict_validation | true    | Enforce all validation rules        |
499: | auto_fix          | false   | Automatically fix formatting issues |
500: | frontmatter_check | true    | Validate frontmatter per document type |
501: ```
502: 
503: **After (YAML Configuration)**:
504: ```yaml
505: feature_flags:
506:   strict_validation:
507:     default: true
508:     description: "Enforce all validation rules without warnings"
509:     values: [true, false]
510: 
511:   auto_fix:
512:     default: false
513:     description: "Automatically fix formatting issues during validation"
514:     values: [true, false]
515:     warning: "Use with caution - may change document semantics"
516: 
517:   frontmatter_check:
518:     default: true
519:     description: "Validate frontmatter fields per document type"
520:     values: [true, false]
521:     enforcement_level: "error"
522: ```
523: 
524: ### YAML Workflow: Multi-Branch Decision Process
525: 
526: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
527: ```markdown
528: The system should detect when to generate variants:
529: - If user explicitly requests options (shows me options, variations, different approaches)
530: - If complexity is high (7+) and uncertainty signals are present (not sure, what would work)
531: - Otherwise, generate single solution
532: 
533: Variant count depends on complexity:
534: - Simple: 2-3 variants
535: - Standard: 3-5 variants
536: - Complex: 5-10 variants
537: ```
538: 
539: **After (YAML Multi-Branch)**:
540: ```yaml
541: variant_generation_logic:
542:   triggers:
543:     explicit:
544:       keywords: ["show me options", "variations", "different approaches", "multiple designs"]
545:       action: "Generate variants immediately"
546:       priority: "high"
547: 
548:     implicit:
549:       conditions:
550:         - "complexity >= 7"
551:         - "uncertainty_signals present"
552:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work", "best approach"]
553:       action: "Generate variants with uncertainty disclaimer"
554:       priority: "medium"
555: 
556:     default:
557:       action: "Generate single optimal solution"
558:       priority: "low"
559: 
560:   variant_count_guidelines:
561:     simple:
562:       complexity_range: [1, 3]
563:       variant_count: "2-3"
564: 
565:     standard:
566:       complexity_range: [4, 6]
567:       variant_count: "3-5"
568: 
569:     complex:
570:       complexity_range: [7, 10]
571:       variant_count: "5-10"
572: 
573:     user_specified:
574:       action: "Honor user's requested count"
575:       override: true
576: ```

578: ---
579: 
580: ## 8. CONFIGURATION TEMPLATES
581: 
582: **Purpose**: Demonstrate structured data formats for configuration and metadata.
583: 
584: ### YAML: Tool Configuration
585:

674: 
675: ## 9. TEMPLATE GUIDELINES
676:

42: ## 2. OVERVIEW

44: ### Why This Skill Exists
45: 
46: Documentation drifts without a standard. Section order wanders. Frontmatter goes missing. Voice slides into filler and one author's README reads nothing like the next. A reader re-learns the layout every time. An AI assistant cannot parse the structure reliably. Hand-checking every document against a style guide does not scale and misses things.
47: 
48: sk-doc makes structure the first gate so these problems never reach production. The script catches what is wrong before the AI touches a line. A reader opens any changelog, any skill README or any flowchart and knows exactly where to look and what to expect. An AI assistant loads a document and finds the same landmarks every time.
49: 
50: ### What It Does
51: 
52: sk-doc is the single specialist for documentation and OpenCode components. Its core pipeline extracts a document to JSON with a quality score, a pass or fail checklist, a list of violations and the evaluation questions the AI answers, all computed before the AI judges the content. Beyond quality enforcement it scaffolds and packages skills, agents, commands and other OpenCode components, with validation as the gate before any package ships. It authors benchmark packages with deterministic conformance inputs for peer adapters, then builds ASCII flowcharts, feature catalogs that inventory current behavior and manual testing playbooks that prove it. Its sk-create-diff packet compares two versions of a document (text, Markdown, HTML, DOCX or text-PDF) without Git and renders the changes as a self-contained, zero-JavaScript HTML report with section-aware navigation. Its sk-create-with-human-voice packet applies the Human Voice Rules to prose: a scope gate that names what a voice edit may not touch, a scanner that parses the standard at run time rather than carrying a copy, a judgment pass no scanner can perform, and a re-scan that proves the rewrite landed. Its sk-create-goal packet authors a spec packet's `goal.md` from a template for its kind and checks the result against the goal contract before handing over the chat slice.

97: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
98: 
99: ### The Structure-First Pipeline
100: 
101: Every document passes through the same sequence. The script parses the markdown, extracts the heading tree along with the frontmatter and the code blocks, runs the checklist for the detected document type and computes the three-component DQI. It outputs flat JSON. The AI reads that JSON and answers the evaluation questions the script poses, then produces ranked recommendations. No document gets a quality pass without the script running first.
102: 
103: ### The DQI
104: 
105: The Documentation Quality Index scores a document from 0 to 100 across three components:
106: 
107: | Component | Points | What it covers |
108: |---|---|---|
109: | Structure | 40 | checklist pass rate, heading hierarchy and section completeness |
110: | Content | 30 | word count in the right range, heading density, code examples, links and tables |
111: | Style | 30 | H2 format, section dividers, intro paragraph and HVR compliance |
112: 
113: The four bands tell you where you stand:
114: 
115: | Band | Score | What it means |
116: |---|---|---|
117: | Excellent | 90 to 100 | Production-ready, nothing to fix |
118: | Good | 75 to 89 | Shareable, minor improvements recommended |
119: | Acceptable | 60 to 74 | Functional but several areas need attention |
120: | Needs Work | Below 60 | Not ready, fix in priority order |
121: 
122: ### Scripts Versus AI
123: 
124: The scripts own the deterministic work. `extract_structure.py` parses, measures, checks and reports. `validate_document.py` gates format at the exit-code level. `init_skill.py` scaffolds a directory. `package_skill.py` validates and bundles. `quick_validate.py` runs fast naming and frontmatter checks. The AI owns the quality judgment: it reads the JSON, evaluates content depth and clarity, scores style against the Human Voice Rules and writes the recommendations. The split keeps the metrics repeatable and the judgment human-sounding. The Node scripts get their one dependency, `@spec-kit/shared`, from the `package.json` at the skill root, which sits there rather than under `scripts/` so that both `scripts/` and `shared/scripts/` can resolve it.

24: 
25: # sk-doc
26: 
27: > Document quality starts with structure. A deterministic script extracts and scores a document before a human or an AI judges it, so every document of a given type ships in the same shape and clears the same bar.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
32: 
33: | Aspect | What you get |
34: |---|---|
35: | **Use it for** | Markdown quality enforcement, human-voice passes, component scaffolding and packaging, benchmark authoring, diagrams, charts, flowcharts, feature catalogs, testing playbooks, changelogs, repo rules, frontmatter contracts and local before/after document diffs |
36: | **Invoke with** | "create a skill", "validate doc", "conformance benchmark", "readme", "documentation", "flowchart", "create a chart", "create a diagram", "repo rule", "frontmatter contract", "apply human voice", "changelog" or Gate 2 auto-routing on documentation keywords |
37: | **Works on** | Markdown files, OpenCode components (skills, agents, commands), standalone HTML diagrams/charts and ASCII flowcharts |
38: | **Produces** | DQI scores, validated documents, packaged skill zips, templated component directories, standalone HTML diagrams/charts and self-contained HTML diff reports |
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ## 2. OVERVIEW
43: 
44: ### Why This Skill Exists
45: 
46: Documentation drifts without a standard. Section order wanders. Frontmatter goes missing. Voice slides into filler and one author's README reads nothing like the next. A reader re-learns the layout every time. An AI assistant cannot parse the structure reliably. Hand-checking every document against a style guide does not scale and misses things.
47: 
48: sk-doc makes structure the first gate so these problems never reach production. The script catches what is wrong before the AI touches a line. A reader opens any changelog, any skill README or any flowchart and knows exactly where to look and what to expect. An AI assistant loads a document and finds the same landmarks every time.
49: 
50: ### What It Does
51: 
52: sk-doc is the single specialist for documentation and OpenCode components. Its core pipeline extracts a document to JSON with a quality score, a pass or fail checklist, a list of violations and the evaluation questions the AI answers, all computed before the AI judges the content. Beyond quality enforcement it scaffolds and packages skills, agents, commands and other OpenCode components, with validation as the gate before any package ships. It authors benchmark packages with deterministic conformance inputs for peer adapters, then builds ASCII flowcharts, feature catalogs that inventory current behavior and manual testing playbooks that prove it. Its sk-create-diff packet compares two versions of a document (text, Markdown, HTML, DOCX or text-PDF) without Git and renders the changes as a self-contained, zero-JavaScript HTML report with section-aware navigation. Its sk-create-with-human-voice packet applies the Human Voice Rules to prose: a scope gate that names what a voice edit may not touch, a scanner that parses the standard at run time rather than carrying a copy, a judgment pass no scanner can perform, and a re-scan that proves the rewrite landed. Its sk-create-goal packet authors a spec packet's `goal.md` from a template for its kind and checks the result against the goal contract before handing over the chat slice.
53: 
54: It does not own code or spec folders. `sk-code` owns code standards and tests. `system-spec-kit` owns the spec-folder lifecycle together with memory and continuity. The two skills touch markdown but do not overlap: sk-doc judges document quality and system-spec-kit enforces the spec-packet contract.
55: 
56: ### The Type-Aware Enforcement Layer
57: 
58: The validator reads the file path and content shape, then applies the matching enforcement level automatically. The detected type decides the strictness.
59: 
60: | Document class | Enforcement level |
61: |---|---|
62: | SKILL and command docs | Strict, with blocking violations that stop the gate |
63: | README docs | Usability-focused, with safe auto-fixes only and no blocking rules beyond the essential sections |
64: | Knowledge docs | Moderately strict |
65: | Active spec docs | Loose unless the task explicitly asks for enforcement |
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 3. QUICK START
70: 
71: **Step 1: Invoke it.** Gate 2 auto-routing fires on documentation keywords. Otherwise read the skill directly.
72: 
73: ```bash
74: python3 .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py "validate my README" --threshold 0.8
75: ```
76: 
77: The advisor prints a routing recommendation with a score. A score above the 0.8 threshold names sk-doc as the skill to load.
78: 
79: **Step 2: Score a document.** `extract_structure.py` returns the DQI, the checklist results, every violation and the evaluation questions in JSON.
80: 
81: ```bash
82: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/extract_structure.py <path/to/document.md>
83: ```
84: 
85: Success looks like a JSON object with `dqi.total`, `dqi.band` and `checklist.passed`. A band of "excellent" or "good" means the document is ready. A band of "needs_work" means the checklist output tells you exactly what to fix and in what order.
86: 
87: **Step 3: Validate a README before delivery.** `validate_document.py` is the fast gate. It checks required sections, heading format and frontmatter.
88: 
89: ```bash
90: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/validate_document.py README.md --type readme
91: ```
92: 
93: Exit 0 means the document is valid and ready to ship. Exit 1 means a blocking format error, so fix the reported violations and re-run. Exit 2 means the file could not be read, so check the path.
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
98: 
99: ### The Structure-First Pipeline
100: 
101: Every document passes through the same sequence. The script parses the markdown, extracts the heading tree along with the frontmatter and the code blocks, runs the checklist for the detected document type and computes the three-component DQI. It outputs flat JSON. The AI reads that JSON and answers the evaluation questions the script poses, then produces ranked recommendations. No document gets a quality pass without the script running first.
102: 
103: ### The DQI
104: 
105: The Documentation Quality Index scores a document from 0 to 100 across three components:
106: 
107: | Component | Points | What it covers |
108: |---|---|---|
109: | Structure | 40 | checklist pass rate, heading hierarchy and section completeness |
110: | Content | 30 | word count in the right range, heading density, code examples, links and tables |
111: | Style | 30 | H2 format, section dividers, intro paragraph and HVR compliance |
112: 
113: The four bands tell you where you stand:
114: 
115: | Band | Score | What it means |
116: |---|---|---|
117: | Excellent | 90 to 100 | Production-ready, nothing to fix |
118: | Good | 75 to 89 | Shareable, minor improvements recommended |
119: | Acceptable | 60 to 74 | Functional but several areas need attention |
120: | Needs Work | Below 60 | Not ready, fix in priority order |
121: 
122: ### Scripts Versus AI
123: 
124: The scripts own the deterministic work. `extract_structure.py` parses, measures, checks and reports. `validate_document.py` gates format at the exit-code level. `init_skill.py` scaffolds a directory. `package_skill.py` validates and bundles. `quick_validate.py` runs fast naming and frontmatter checks. The AI owns the quality judgment: it reads the JSON, evaluates content depth and clarity, scores style against the Human Voice Rules and writes the recommendations. The split keeps the metrics repeatable and the judgment human-sounding. The Node scripts get their one dependency, `@spec-kit/shared`, from the `package.json` at the skill root, which sits there rather than under `scripts/` so that both `scripts/` and `shared/scripts/` can resolve it.
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## 5. INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION
129: 
130: ### When To Use This Skill
131: 
132: Reach for sk-doc when you create or edit a markdown document, when you scaffold a skill, an agent, a command or another OpenCode component and when you need a quality gate before publishing. Use it when you build a feature catalog, a testing playbook, a flowchart, a changelog, a spec packet goal or a before/after diff of an edited document. Use it too when a document's DQI score drops and you need to know what to fix and why.
133: 
134: You reach it through thirteen `/create:*` commands: `/create:agent`, `/create:skill`, `/create:skill-parent`, `/create:command`, `/create:feature-catalog`, `/create:manual-testing-playbook`, `/create:benchmark`, `/create:readme`, `/create:changelog`, `/create:diff`, `/create:repo-rule`, `/create:with-human-voice` and `/create:goal`. The `@markdown` agent handles template-first documentation authoring for these and other markdown targets.
135: 
136: Skip sk-doc when the task belongs to a neighbor:
137: 
138: - Code changes route to `sk-code`.
139: - Spec-folder lifecycle operations route to `system-spec-kit`.
140: - Git workflow orchestration routes to `sk-git`.
141: 
142: ### Related Skills
143: 
144: | Skill | Relationship |
145: |---|---|
146: | `sk-code` | Owns code standards and tests. sk-doc documents the skill and validates its README. |
147: | `system-spec-kit` | Owns spec folders, memory and continuity. sk-doc judges quality. The two do not overlap. |
148: | `sk-git` | Owns git workflow. sk-doc produces the commit and PR text quality. |
149: 
150: ---
151: 
152: ## 6. TROUBLESHOOTING
153: 
154: | What you see | Why | Fix |
155: |---|---|---|
156: | DQI below 60 ("needs_work") | Missing sections, no frontmatter on a strict file or multiple HVR violations | Fix in priority order: structure and section order first, then missing sections, then content density, then style. Re-run after each batch. |
157: | `validate_document.py` exits 1 | A blocking format issue: missing required H2, non-sequential numbering or malformed frontmatter | Read the error message line by line. Fix each reported violation and re-run. |
158: | `package_skill.py` fails | SKILL.md is over the 5000-word ceiling, a required section is missing or a subdirectory was not scaffolded | Run `extract_structure.py` on SKILL.md first. Move deep detail into `references/` files if the word count is too high. |
159: | Wrong document type detected | The file path or content shape misled the detector, or no type rule matched and README rules were applied, which prints a `document_type_fallback` warning | Check the detected type in the JSON output. Override with `--type` on `validate_document.py`. |
160: 
161: ---
162: 
163: ## 7. FAQ
164: 
165: **Q: When do I use sk-doc instead of system-spec-kit? Both touch markdown.**
166: 
167: A: sk-doc judges document quality and creates components. system-spec-kit owns the spec-packet contract: Level 1 requires `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md` and `implementation-summary.md`. Level 2 adds `acceptance-criteria.md` as the closure gate. Packet metadata also includes `description.json` and `graph-metadata.json` for phase parents and save/resume state. The two do not overlap. Use sk-doc for a README, a skill scaffold, a changelog or any markdown component. Use system-spec-kit when you start a spec-folder-tracked change.
168: 
169: **Q: `validate_document.py` and `extract_structure.py`: which one do I run?**
170: 
171: A: Run `validate_document.py` as the fast delivery gate for README files. It exits 0 or 1 and checks only the formatting rules that block publishing. Run `extract_structure.py` when you want the full picture: the DQI score, the checklist pass rate, the violations and the evaluation questions. It works on any markdown document type. Use both in sequence.
172: 
173: **Q: What is the difference between a feature catalog and a manual testing playbook?**
174: 
175: A: A feature catalog documents current behavior. It inventories what a skill or system can do, organized by numbered categories, with source-file anchors and stable slugs. A testing playbook defines how to test that behavior manually, with deterministic prompts, expected signals, evidence requirements and a cross-reference back to the catalog. The catalog is the stable capability reference. The playbook links back to it through a cross-reference index. A playbook scenario is either a single prompt an operator runs and judges, or a scripted conversation the shared runner plays into live runtimes when the result depends on a later answer, turn or restart. Build the catalog first.
176: 
177: **Q: Which `/create:*` command do I use?**
178: 
179: A: `/create:skill` for a new skill under `.skilled/skills/`. `/create:skill-parent` for a parent skill with nested mode packets. `/create:agent` for an agent under `.skilled/agents/`. `/create:command` for an OpenCode slash command set. `/create:feature-catalog` for a rooted feature inventory. `/create:manual-testing-playbook` for a manual testing package. `/create:benchmark` for MCP promotion and family-keyed benchmark authoring. `/design:diagram` for an HTML/SVG technical diagram or a validated ASCII/markdown flowchart. `/design:chart` for a standalone HTML chart drawn from the catalog of chart forms. `/create:readme` for a directory-level README. `/create:changelog` for a versioned changelog entry. `/create:diff` for a git-free before/after document review. `/create:repo-rule` for a repo-local rule wired into `REPO RULES.md`. `/create:with-human-voice` to apply or score the Human Voice Rules over prose. `/create:goal` for a spec packet's `goal.md`.
180: 
181: ---
182: 
183: ## 8. VERIFICATION
184: 
185: The skill ships the checks that prove a document is ready.

188: |---|---|
189: | README structure | `python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/validate_document.py README.md --type readme` reports zero issues and exits 0 |
190: | Full quality | `python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/extract_structure.py <document.md>` returns the DQI, the checklist and the violations in JSON |

194:

12: # Documentation Authoring Hub (sk-doc)

14: One advisor identity, fifteen workflow modes across fourteen packets, one shared sk-create-quality-control backbone.

16: It holds NO per-packet logic: it routes by `workflowMode` through `mode-registry.json`, and each packet keeps its own contract in its nested folder.

35: router picks the LEAVES within it. The two layers stay separate — the hub never
36: emits leaf paths, and this router never re-decides the mode.

39: ## 2. INTENT MODEL
40: 
41: - **doc-quality leaves** — the validation rules, core standards, evergreen
42:   packet-id rule, and the quality-control workflow a request to validate, audit,
43:   or score documentation against sk-doc standards loads. Fired by "documentation
44:   quality / validate documentation / validate a document / score this document /
45:   DQI / document audit / review the docs / audit the docs / pass review"
46:   requests. The scoring phrases mirror `hub-router.json`, so a request that
47:   reaches the quality mode at stage one also reaches its leaves at stage two.
48: - **optimization leaves** — the optimization reference and the llms.txt templates
49:   a request to compress, trim, or token-optimize a doc, or emit a machine-readable
50:   index loads. Fired by "optimize / token efficiency / llms.txt / reduce tokens /
51:   slim down" requests.
52: - **skill-creation leaves** — the skill creation workflow and the skill.md /
53:   readme / reference templates a request to scaffold or author a new skill loads.
54:   Fired by "create a skill / skill.md scaffold / resource_map wiring / package a
55:   capability" requests.
56: - **parent-hub leaves.** The nested-packet contract, the hub-router schema and
57:   the four parent-hub templates a request to build or rewire a parent hub loads.
58:   Fired by "parent hub / parent skill / mode packet / nested workflow packet /
59:   mode-registry.json / hub-router.json" requests, the file names spelled in full
60:   so a bare "hub router" in an unrelated sentence does not fire it. This is the leaf set for the
61:   `sk-create-skill-parent` mode, which shares the `sk-create-skill` packet but
62:   not its leaves: a plain skill request must not pull the hub templates.
63: - **agent-creation leaves.** The agent README and agent template a request to
64:   scaffold an OpenCode agent loads. Fired by "create an agent / new agent /
65:   agent frontmatter / permission object / @analyze agent" requests.
66: - **command-creation leaves.** The command README and command template a
67:   request to scaffold a slash command loads. Fired by "create a command / slash
68:   command / argument-hint / allowed-tools / thin router" requests.
69: - **agent-command leaves.** Both packets' READMEs and templates a request to
70:   author an agent together with its paired `/create` command loads. Fired only
71:   by the two paired phrases, "agent and paired" and "paired /create", which no
72:   single-artifact request carries. The paired intent stays separate rather than
73:   being expressed as the union of the two above, because the router keeps only
74:   intents within one point of the top score: a paired request that also names
75:   the agent would otherwise drop the command half.
76: - **diagram and chart leaves belong to the `sk-design` hub.** ASCII flowchart,
77:   decision-tree and standalone HTML chart authoring is `sk-design-diagram` and
78:   `sk-design-chart` work, and this router declares no intent for it: `/design:diagram`
79:   and `/design:chart` are the entry points, so "flowchart", "ascii", "process diagram",
80:   "create a chart" and "plot the data" reach no key in the two maps below.
81: - **human-voice leaves** — the scope gate, the scoring method and the Human
82:   Voice Rules standard a request to apply or score that standard loads. Fired
83:   by "hvr / human voice rules / apply human voice / rewrite in human voice /
84:   make this sound human / sounds ai-generated / remove ai tells" requests. The
85:   scope gate is the always-loaded leaf, because deciding what a voice edit may
86:   touch comes before deciding what to change.
87: - **playbook leaves** — the manual-testing-playbook README a request to author a
88:   manual testing playbook loads. Fired by "playbook system / manual testing
89:   playbook / testing playbook / playbook scenario / manual test
90:   scenario" requests.
91: - **playbook-conversation leaves** — the conversation-scenario reference and the
92:   conversation snippet template a request to write a multi-turn json conversation script for
93:   a playbook scenario loads. Fired by "playbook conversation / multi-turn
94:   conversation script / json conversation / conversation runner" requests. This
95:   intent scores double. "manual testing playbook" also matches "testing
96:   playbook", so that one phrase scores the playbook intent twice, and at equal
97:   weight a request naming both a playbook and a conversation would load only the
98:   playbook README. At double weight the two tie and both leaf sets load.
99: - **feature-catalog leaves** — the feature-catalog README a request to inventory a
100:   project's features / capabilities loads. Fired by "feature catalog / feature
101:   inventory / capabilities" requests.
102: - **readme-creation leaves** — the readme README and readme template a request to
103:   author a project README / front-page overview loads. Fired by "create a readme /
104:   readme for / project overview / landing doc" requests.
105: - **changelog leaves** — the changelog template a request to author release notes
106:   / version notes loads. Fired by "changelog / release notes / what shipped /
107:   since the last version" requests.
108: - **benchmark leaves** — the benchmark shared README, worked example, and report
109:   template a request to author a behavior benchmark
110:   loads. Fired by "create a benchmark / benchmark suite / behavior benchmark"
111:   requests.
112: - **diff leaves** — the diff README, workflow, and worked example a request to
113:   produce a before/after document diff loads. Fired by "document diff / before
114:   and after diff / visual document diff" requests.
115: - **repo-rule leaves** — the four decision tests, the rule anatomy contract, the
116:   creation standards, the wiring contract, the rule and router templates, and the
117:   packet reference map a
118:   request to add, change, or remove a repo-local rule loads. Fired by "repo rule /
119:   project rule / REPO RULES.md / trigger table / retire a repo rule" requests. Most such
120:   requests end in a refusal, so `decision-tests.md` is the always-loaded leaf.
121: - **frontmatter leaves** — the field reference and the versioning standard a
122:   request about a frontmatter block itself loads. Fired by "yaml frontmatter /
123:   frontmatter block / frontmatter field / description budget / 4-part version /
124:   frontmatter versioning" requests. The phrases are qualified rather than bare,
125:   because `agent frontmatter` belongs to agent-creation and a bare "frontmatter"
126:   would take that route away from it. The field reference is the always-loaded
127:   leaf, because resolving the document class comes before any field rule.
128: - **goal-authoring leaves** — the goal authoring standards, the goal exemplars,
129:   the parent/nested goal workflows and the budget/handoff reference a request to
130:   author or revise a packet's `goal.md` loads. Fired by "packet goal / goal.md /
131:   goal document / author goal.md / phase parent goal / goal criteria /
132:   completion checks" requests. The phrases are qualified rather than bare,
133:   because a bare "goal" and the session verbs belong to session-goal management
134:   (set, bind, update, resend), which the goal hooks and host commands own. The
135:   authoring standards are the always-loaded leaf, because what a goal must state
136:   comes before how one is phrased.
137: - **full-inventory leaves** — the entire sk-doc toolkit. `FULL_INVENTORY` is the
138:   single explicit full-toolkit intent; no other intent enumerates the whole hub.
139:   Fired only by an explicit "show the full sk-doc toolkit / everything sk-doc
140:   offers" request.
141: 
142: A single dominant documentation axis routes to one mode's leaf set; two clearly
143: separate axes route to both.

408: 
409: ## 4. HOW TO READ THIS
410: 
411: - One dominant intent routes to one mode's leaf set.
412: - Two near-tied intents (within the ambiguity delta) route to both leaf sets; the
413:   union is deduped by canonical pair.
414: - No keyword match is UNKNOWN_FALLBACK: confirm the target artifact and intent
415:   before loading anything.
416: - `FULL_INVENTORY` fires only on an explicit "show the whole toolkit" request.
417: 
418: ---
419: 
420: ## 5. MACHINE ROUTER
421: 
422: The hub's detailed routing prose, moved here from `SKILL.md` so the skill body keeps only a short routing summary and a pointer to this file. It sits last, after the stage-two map above, and it declares no map of its own: the `INTENT_SIGNALS` and `RESOURCE_MAP` block in section 3 stays the only replay source.
423: 
424: > **Compiled routing (default-on, flag-gated, additive).** Resolve the mode via the compiled router contract first:
425: > ```bash
426: > node .skilled/bin/compiled-route.cjs --hub sk-doc --prompt "<task>"
427: > ```
428: > Follow the returned decision — `route` (use its `targets`), `clarify`/`defer` (disambiguate), `reject` (refuse). On a `{"servingAuthority":"legacy"}` sentinel or any error, use the routing below. The front door self-gates on serving-authority. Compiled routing is now the default for `sk-doc`; set `SPECKIT_COMPILED_ROUTING=0` to force legacy routing fleet-wide — the explicit kill-switch.
429: 
430: ### Surface Router — per-intent leaf sets
431: 
432: Stage 2 of routing lives in section 3 of this file.
433: It defines three things:
434: - The per-intent leaf model: document quality, optimization, skill creation, parent-hub creation, agent creation, command creation, the paired agent-plus-command lane, flowcharts, the human-voice pass, playbooks, feature catalogs, READMEs, changelogs, benchmarks, diffs, packet goals, repo rules, and the explicit full-toolkit intent.
435: - The machine-readable `INTENT_SIGNALS` / `RESOURCE_MAP` block that the deterministic router-replay and benchmarks parse.
436: - The how-to-read rules: a dominant intent gives one leaf set, near-tied intents give a deduped union, and no keyword match gives the hub UNKNOWN fallback, never a silent default.
437: 
438: Every `RESOURCE_MAP` path is packet-qualified or an authored shared-alias disk path, and each converts to the canonical `(workflowMode, leafResourceId)` pair at the one contract boundary.
439: 
440: The reason this file stays a separate document from `SKILL.md` and from `hub-router.json` is in [the parent-skill reference](sk-create-skill/references/parent-skill/parent-skills-nested-packets.md#why-the-leaf-router-stays-in-routermd).
441: 
442: ### The discriminator
443: - **`workflowMode`** — the public packet key (e.g. `sk-create-skill`, `sk-create-quality-control`). `sk-create-skill-parent` is a second mode over the same `sk-create-skill` packet.
444: - **`packetKind`** — `workflow` for every sk-doc packet (there is no surface axis; the sk-create-quality-control pipeline is universal doctrine in `shared/`, not orthogonal stack-evidence).
445: - **`backendKind`** — `template-scaffold` for the create-* generators, `sk-create-quality-control` for the sk-create-quality-control mode.
446: 
447: ### Routing rule
448: ```
449: SKILL_ROOT = path containing this ROUTER.md and its SKILL.md
450: REGISTRY = SKILL_ROOT / "mode-registry.json"
451: HUB_ROUTER = SKILL_ROOT / "hub-router.json"
452: 
453: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [
454:     "Confirm whether this is sk-create-skill, sk-create-skill-parent, sk-create-readme, sk-create-agent, sk-create-command, sk-create-feature-catalog, sk-create-manual-testing-playbook, sk-create-benchmark, sk-create-changelog, sk-create-diff, sk-create-repo-rule, sk-create-frontmatter, sk-create-goal, sk-create-with-human-voice, or sk-create-quality-control work",
455:     "Confirm the target document or component being authored, scaffolded, or reviewed",
456:     "Provide the available inputs: existing doc, source material, or scaffold parameters",
457:     "Confirm the validation expectations before completion (DQI/HVR scoring, validate.sh, or packet-specific checks)",
458: ]
459: 
460: def _guard_in_skill(relative_path):
461:   resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
462:   resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)
463:   if resolved.suffix.lower() not in {".md", ".json"}:
464:     raise ValueError("only skill-local markdown/json router resources are routable")
465:   return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()
466: 
467: def load_if_available(relative_path, seen):
468:   guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)
469:   if guarded not in seen and (SKILL_ROOT / guarded).exists():
470:     load(guarded)
471:     seen.add(guarded)
472:     return True
473:   return False
474: 
475: seen = set()
476: if not REGISTRY.exists() or not HUB_ROUTER.exists():
477:   return defer("router metadata missing; inspect sk-doc/mode-registry.json and sk-doc/hub-router.json")
478: 
479: read mode-registry.json and hub-router.json
480: classify the request to one or more workflowMode values using hub-router.json
481:   (dominant authoring/quality intent; a command like /create:agent resolves directly)
482: 
483: if confidence is low, intent is contradictory, or routerPolicy.defaultMode is null and no mode wins:
484:   for resource in hub_router.routerPolicy.defaultResource:   # the ordered defer set, never hardcoded here
485:     load_if_available(resource, seen)
486:   return UNKNOWN_FALLBACK with disambiguation_checklist = UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST
487: 
488: for each resolved workflowMode:
489:   entry = the matching mode-registry.json modes[] item
490:   if entry is missing or entry.packetKind != "workflow":
491:     return defer("unknown sk-doc workflowMode; extend mode-registry.json and create a packet first")
492:   if not load_if_available(f"{entry.packet}/SKILL.md", seen):
493:     return defer("registered packet SKILL.md is missing; repair the packet before routing")
494: 
495: return single or orderedBundle according to hub-router.json routerPolicy.outcomes
496: ```
497: `routerPolicy.defaultMode` is `null`: an unclear documentation intent asks for disambiguation rather than forcing a stale default. `hub-router.json` carries the router signals, vocabulary classes, default fallback resource, and bundle rules. Outcomes are `single`, `orderedBundle`, or `defer` — there is no `surfaceBundle` (no surface axis).
498: 
499: Per-packet behavior is **not flattened**: each packet keeps its own authoring contract, references, assets, scripts, and templates.
500: 
501: This hub does **not** use keyed resource discovery (`references/<key>/` or `assets/<key>/`) at the hub root.
502: There are no hub-root `references/` or `assets/` directories, and packet resources stay inside their owning packet or the shared backbone.
503: If a future workflow needs keyed resource subdirectories, add that behavior inside the owning packet using guarded runtime discovery.
504: Do not hardcode resource inventories in this hub.

14: ---
15: 
16: # sk-doc Surface Router — per-intent leaf sets
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: This is sk-doc's second-layer (surface) router, first-class at the hub root as
21: `ROUTER.md`. The hub selects a workflow mode in [`hub-router.json`](hub-router.json)
22: (sk-create-skill, sk-create-skill-parent, sk-create-readme, sk-create-agent, sk-create-command,
23: sk-create-feature-catalog, sk-create-manual-testing-playbook, sk-create-benchmark,
24: sk-create-changelog, sk-create-diff, sk-create-repo-rule, sk-create-frontmatter,
25: sk-create-goal, sk-create-with-human-voice, or sk-create-quality-control);
26: this doc maps a request's documentation/authoring intent to the exact packet-local
27: leaf resources that mode should load. Every path is either packet-qualified
28: (`<packet>/references|assets/…`) or an authored shared-alias disk path (`shared/…`),
29: and both convert to the canonical `(workflowMode, leafResourceId)` pair at the
30: contract boundary (`sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/lib/leaf-resource-contract.cjs`).
31: `FULL_INVENTORY` is the single explicit full-toolkit intent — no other intent
32: enumerates the whole hub.
33: 
34: Routing is two stages: the hub picks the WORKFLOW mode (mode telemetry), this
35: router picks the LEAVES within it. The two layers stay separate — the hub never
36: emits leaf paths, and this router never re-decides the mode.
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 2. INTENT MODEL
40: 
41: - **doc-quality leaves** — the validation rules, core standards, evergreen
42:   packet-id rule, and the quality-control workflow a request to validate, audit,
43:   or score documentation against sk-doc standards loads. Fired by "documentation
44:   quality / validate documentation / validate a document / score this document /
45:   DQI / document audit / review the docs / audit the docs / pass review"
46:   requests. The scoring phrases mirror `hub-router.json`, so a request that
47:   reaches the quality mode at stage one also reaches its leaves at stage two.
48: - **optimization leaves** — the optimization reference and the llms.txt templates
49:   a request to compress, trim, or token-optimize a doc, or emit a machine-readable
50:   index loads. Fired by "optimize / token efficiency / llms.txt / reduce tokens /
51:   slim down" requests.
52: - **skill-creation leaves** — the skill creation workflow and the skill.md /
53:   readme / reference templates a request to scaffold or author a new skill loads.
54:   Fired by "create a skill / skill.md scaffold / resource_map wiring / package a
55:   capability" requests.
56: - **parent-hub leaves.** The nested-packet contract, the hub-router schema and
57:   the four parent-hub templates a request to build or rewire a parent hub loads.
58:   Fired by "parent hub / parent skill / mode packet / nested workflow packet /
59:   mode-registry.json / hub-router.json" requests, the file names spelled in full
60:   so a bare "hub router" in an unrelated sentence does not fire it. This is the leaf set for the
61:   `sk-create-skill-parent` mode, which shares the `sk-create-skill` packet but
62:   not its leaves: a plain skill request must not pull the hub templates.
63: - **agent-creation leaves.** The agent README and agent template a request to
64:   scaffold an OpenCode agent loads. Fired by "create an agent / new agent /
65:   agent frontmatter / permission object / @analyze agent" requests.
66: - **command-creation leaves.** The command README and command template a
67:   request to scaffold a slash command loads. Fired by "create a command / slash
68:   command / argument-hint / allowed-tools / thin router" requests.
69: - **agent-command leaves.** Both packets' READMEs and templates a request to
70:   author an agent together with its paired `/create` command loads. Fired only
71:   by the two paired phrases, "agent and paired" and "paired /create", which no
72:   single-artifact request carries. The paired intent stays separate rather than
73:   being expressed as the union of the two above, because the router keeps only
74:   intents within one point of the top score: a paired request that also names
75:   the agent would otherwise drop the command half.
76: - **diagram and chart leaves belong to the `sk-design` hub.** ASCII flowchart,
77:   decision-tree and standalone HTML chart authoring is `sk-design-diagram` and
78:   `sk-design-chart` work, and this router declares no intent for it: `/design:diagram`
79:   and `/design:chart` are the entry points, so "flowchart", "ascii", "process diagram",
80:   "create a chart" and "plot the data" reach no key in the two maps below.
81: - **human-voice leaves** — the scope gate, the scoring method and the Human
82:   Voice Rules standard a request to apply or score that standard loads. Fired
83:   by "hvr / human voice rules / apply human voice / rewrite in human voice /
84:   make this sound human / sounds ai-generated / remove ai tells" requests. The
85:   scope gate is the always-loaded leaf, because deciding what a voice edit may
86:   touch comes before deciding what to change.
87: - **playbook leaves** — the manual-testing-playbook README a request to author a
88:   manual testing playbook loads. Fired by "playbook system / manual testing
89:   playbook / testing playbook / playbook scenario / manual test
90:   scenario" requests.
91: - **playbook-conversation leaves** — the conversation-scenario reference and the
92:   conversation snippet template a request to write a multi-turn json conversation script for
93:   a playbook scenario loads. Fired by "playbook conversation / multi-turn
94:   conversation script / json conversation / conversation runner" requests. This
95:   intent scores double. "manual testing playbook" also matches "testing
96:   playbook", so that one phrase scores the playbook intent twice, and at equal
97:   weight a request naming both a playbook and a conversation would load only the
98:   playbook README. At double weight the two tie and both leaf sets load.
99: - **feature-catalog leaves** — the feature-catalog README a request to inventory a
100:   project's features / capabilities loads. Fired by "feature catalog / feature
101:   inventory / capabilities" requests.
102: - **readme-creation leaves** — the readme README and readme template a request to
103:   author a project README / front-page overview loads. Fired by "create a readme /
104:   readme for / project overview / landing doc" requests.
105: - **changelog leaves** — the changelog template a request to author release notes
106:   / version notes loads. Fired by "changelog / release notes / what shipped /
107:   since the last version" requests.
108: - **benchmark leaves** — the benchmark shared README, worked example, and report
109:   template a request to author a behavior benchmark
110:   loads. Fired by "create a benchmark / benchmark suite / behavior benchmark"
111:   requests.
112: - **diff leaves** — the diff README, workflow, and worked example a request to
113:   produce a before/after document diff loads. Fired by "document diff / before
114:   and after diff / visual document diff" requests.
115: - **repo-rule leaves** — the four decision tests, the rule anatomy contract, the
116:   creation standards, the wiring contract, the rule and router templates, and the
117:   packet reference map a
118:   request to add, change, or remove a repo-local rule loads. Fired by "repo rule /
119:   project rule / REPO RULES.md / trigger table / retire a repo rule" requests. Most such
120:   requests end in a refusal, so `decision-tests.md` is the always-loaded leaf.
121: - **frontmatter leaves** — the field reference and the versioning standard a
122:   request about a frontmatter block itself loads. Fired by "yaml frontmatter /
123:   frontmatter block / frontmatter field / description budget / 4-part version /
124:   frontmatter versioning" requests. The phrases are qualified rather than bare,
125:   because `agent frontmatter` belongs to agent-creation and a bare "frontmatter"
126:   would take that route away from it. The field reference is the always-loaded
127:   leaf, because resolving the document class comes before any field rule.
128: - **goal-authoring leaves** — the goal authoring standards, the goal exemplars,
129:   the parent/nested goal workflows and the budget/handoff reference a request to
130:   author or revise a packet's `goal.md` loads. Fired by "packet goal / goal.md /
131:   goal document / author goal.md / phase parent goal / goal criteria /
132:   completion checks" requests. The phrases are qualified rather than bare,
133:   because a bare "goal" and the session verbs belong to session-goal management
134:   (set, bind, update, resend), which the goal hooks and host commands own. The
135:   authoring standards are the always-loaded leaf, because what a goal must state
136:   comes before how one is phrased.
137: - **full-inventory leaves** — the entire sk-doc toolkit. `FULL_INVENTORY` is the
138:   single explicit full-toolkit intent; no other intent enumerates the whole hub.
139:   Fired only by an explicit "show the full sk-doc toolkit / everything sk-doc
140:   offers" request.
141: 
142: A single dominant documentation axis routes to one mode's leaf set; two clearly
143: separate axes route to both.
